scenes.vo: Imagine paying ten thousand guilders for one single flower bulb.
scenes.label: for ONE tulip bulb

scenes.vo: In Amsterdam, that was about the price of a fine house on a canal.
This is the story of Tulip Mania, the most famous bubble in history.
scenes.title: Tulip Mania

scenes.vo: In the sixteen thirties, the Dutch Republic was one of the richest places on Earth.
scenes.caption: The Dutch Golden Age

scenes.vo: Its ships brought spices, silk and silver from across the world, and people had money to spend.
scenes.text: Spices. Silk. Silver. Money to spend.

scenes.vo: Tulips had arrived from the Ottoman Empire, and by the sixteen thirties, the Dutch were obsessed with them.
The most wanted were the broken tulips, with flames of colour on their petals.
scenes.caption: The 'broken' tulips

scenes.vo: Nobody knew it then, but those beautiful flames were caused by a virus.
Back then, a skilled craftsman earned about three hundred guilders a year.
scenes.label: a craftsman's pay, for a whole YEAR

scenes.vo: So one rare bulb could cost more than thirty years of his wages.
scenes.title: Guilders

scenes.vo: In winter, the bulbs were still in the ground. So people traded something else: paper promises.
scenes.caption: Paper promises

scenes.vo: The Dutch called it the wind trade: deals made in taverns, for flowers nobody could see.
Prices climbed week after week, because every buyer hoped to sell to someone who would pay even more. Then, in February sixteen thirty seven, everything stopped.
scenes.title: Bulb price (illustration)

scenes.vo: At a bulb sale in Haarlem, the buyers simply did not show up.
scenes.caption: Haarlem, February 1637

scenes.vo: Within days, the bulbs had lost most of their value.
scenes.text: Within days: most of the value, gone.

scenes.vo: Buyers were left with contracts they did not want to pay, for flowers nobody wanted any more.
scenes.title: What was left

scenes.vo: Two hundred years later, a famous book told it as a story of national madness.
But modern historians found that the story was exaggerated. Few people were truly ruined, and the Dutch economy kept growing.
So remember: the price was ten thousand guilders. The value was one flower.
Every bubble starts with a beautiful story. And it usually ends the same way.
scenes.title: Every bubble has a story
